newsitem.title: UK: EU decisions would be hard to reverse-UK's Major.
newsitem.headline: EU decisions would be hard to reverse-UK's Major.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major said he was against the idea of further integration with the European Union because the decisions it took were very hard to reverse.

"I don't believe there is an appetite in the British nation as a whole for more integration in Europe, for more decisions (currently) taken at Westminster to be taken in Europe," he told a local radio station in northern England.

"If decisions are taken in Europe they can be very difficult to reverse. If they are taken in Westminster, they can be corrected. We can change something which we got wrong. That is why I do not want to integrate any further," he said.
Major was reacting to a speech by European Commission President Jacques Santer, who urged nations sceptical about further EU integration not to derail progress and to be as constructive as possible.

Santer said it would be a catastrophe if the EU's Intergovernmental Conference, which is charting the future course of the 15-nation bloc, did not come to a successful conclusion in Amsterdam in June.
Conservative party sources said Major was redrafting part of speech due to be delivered in York later on Monday to take Santer's speech into account.

"The speech...reinforces the fears I first expressed at the press conference (today) about what people want to do at Amsterdam," he told the radio station. Earlier he said his Conservative party opposed the idea of a centralised Europe.
